record.name: Samoa
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. Samoa has done a Digital Readiness Assessment (per UNDP) and takes part in an Australian-funded responsible-AI programme, but no national AI strategy or evaluation body was found.

related_bodies.name: Pacific Islands Forum (regional AI principles and planned governance framework)
related_bodies.role: Leaders endorsed regional AI principles in September 2026 and a regional AI Governance Framework is to be considered in 2027; this is a regional process, not a national body. This was reported by Pacific Islands News Association (PINA).

next_check.reason: Whether a national AI strategy or any national AI evaluation body is adopted.

partial.scope: Negative-status confidence, preserved query provenance, national/official-language search coverage and source-independence audit; this is not a full recheck of all record fields.

Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. The retrieved material does not sufficiently establish the national AI governance arrangements. No new search or full recheck.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.

Re-ran searches in English for a government-designated institute that evaluates advanced models, or a commitment, proposal or study naming one. No qualifying institute or commitment was identified; results described the National ICT Policy and National Cybersecurity Strategy launched in April 2026 and the November 2025 AI-risk workshop with UNDP. Retrieved the communications ministry's National ICT Policy and its launch announcement as new primary governance evidence. Raised confidence to medium under the status-confidence rule: recorded queries in English and a national or official language, and cited primary governance evidence consistent with no qualifying institute. Partial check; the last full-check date is unchanged.

Samoa national artificial intelligence policy Ministry of Communications and Information Technology 2026
Samoa AI safety institute evaluation advanced AI models government

check.language_note: English is an official language or an official language of national administration; it is a practical national search language for this check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. On 24 October 2026 the record was searched again in English; the result links of each query were matched against registered sources in the same way.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: The UNDP and Standards Australia sources concern regional readiness and adoption programmes; meaningful Samoa-specific institute evidence from two independent origins was not established. Confidence was low under that rule; none_identified is a bounded search finding, not proof of absence.
check.governance_note: The National ICT Policy 2025/26-2030/31, launched by the government in April 2026, commits to using AI responsibly to maximise public value and to strengthening and updating regulatory frameworks for emerging technologies, AI among them, in coordination with the regulator, to manage risks while enabling innovation. It names no body to evaluate advanced models.

record.notes: MCIT announced an AI-risk workshop with UNDP in November 2025 covering cyberattacks, fraud and misinformation. UNDP and Standards Australia report the digital-readiness and regional-programme context. No qualifying national evaluation body was identified in the bounded search; workshop activity does not establish one. The earlier search covered English terms for a national AI strategy, AI agency or regulator, and AI safety or testing institute in 2024-2026; other national languages were not comprehensively searched. The earlier ministry-homepage check found no AI policy and the UNDP Samoa AI page was blocked; the later ministry workshop page supplies the additional evidence described here.
